surface_mechanism_description: The surface reactions involve the adsorption of trimethylaluminum (AlMe3) and trimethylgallium (GaMe3) precursors followed by plasma-assisted surface reactions. The self-limiting growth mechanism is achieved through the sequential adsorption and reaction of the precursors with surface hydroxyl groups, leading to the formation of Al-O-Al and Ga-O-Al bonds. The reaction is further facilitated by the plasma environment, which enhances the reactivity of the precursors and enables the formation of nitride layers.
evidence: The text describes the use of hollow cathode plasma-assisted atomic layer deposition (HCPA-ALD) for the deposition of AlN, GaN, and AlxGa1/C0 xN thin films. It mentions the self-limiting growth mechanism, where the adsorption and reaction of trimethylaluminum (AlMe3) and trimethylgallium (GaMe3) precursors with surface hydroxyl groups are key steps. The plasma environment enhances the reactivity of the precursors, leading to the formation of nitride layers through surface reactions involving Al-O-Al and Ga-O-Al bonds.
